title: The Dog Night, 2004
venue: Arthur's site (newspaper cadence: six dailies + a Sunday)
logline: Five years. In color. The bulb is yellow now; it was always yellow.

panels.composition: The dumpster, night, in muddy color: the bulb a warm smear, the dumpster rust, the chain-link gray. WOOD and BARNABY.

image.prompt: a young man and a small dog behind a bowling alley at night before a rusted dumpster under a bare yellow bulb, muddy digital color for the first time in this recurring scene, no words

panels.composition: The rope loop. Gone. Just the chain-link. Wood's hand where it was.

image.prompt: close-up of a hand touching a chain-link fence where a loop of rope used to be, no words
image.notes: The rope is gone this year. Nobody says so.

panels.composition: The dog, five, sitting, gray coming in on the muzzle. Drawn honestly.

image.prompt: close-up of a scruffy dog sitting under a bulb with gray beginning on its muzzle, honest and tender, no words

panels.composition: Walking away. The neon: SMALL WOOD LANES, all lit, in color — pink and blue, cheap, beautiful.

image.prompt: a young man and a dog walking away under a bowling alley's neon sign in cheap pink and blue, all letters lit, night, watercolor, no words

art.line: brush-pen scanned; muddy early-digital flats begin
art.palette: limited, muddy; Sundays in over-wet watercolor
